Open-source generative UI framework: agents stream layout data, and apps render it with native components in React, Angular, Lit, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.

https://a2ui.org/

A2UI

Build delightful, fast, reliable agentic experiences

A2UI (Agent-to-User Interface) is an open-source generative UI framework, complete with a protocol optimized for streaming dynamic user interfaces at low latency, native renderers for web and mobile frameworks, and agent SDKs in several popular languages. With A2UI, your agents can communicate with your users using natively rendered widgets, in addition to text.

Examples of UI compositions that A2UI can express.

Quick links

  • Main website.
  • Try it in your browser using A2UI Composer.
  • Supported renderers.
  • Supported agents.
  • Protocol specification.

Introduction

Large language models (LLMs) and decision models (e.g. Jev) excel at creating text and code and at making fast decisions on top of raw structured data (e.g. JSON). A2UI gives these models a specialized vocabulary for expressing user interfaces.

A2UI expresses UI using data, not code. A schema for the data exchanged between the agent and the renderer enforces strict capability boundaries for the agent, keeping agent-generated experiences safe and aligned with the business requirements of your application. A core library, a native framework adapter, and a catalog of components provide access to native components and form the building blocks that the agent composes into a final user experience, making the result expressive and high-performance.

When to use A2UI

Use A2UI when any of the following apply to your application:

  • Parts of your application are agent- and/or server-driven. By design, A2UI supports remote rendering.
  • You want the UI to be composed dynamically, tailored to the user's immediate need. Instead of making your users navigate through multiple screens to solve their problems, have the agent build the right flow of UI that guides users directly to solutions.
  • You need the highest performance and visual fidelity. A2UI renders UI using the framework of your choice, typically one that the host app itself is written in. WebViews or HTML are not required.
  • The same agent streams UI to multiple platforms or frameworks, such as Flutter, React, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose. A2UI helps keep the user experience compatible and consistent across all screens.
  • The agent is remote, third-party, or operates across a trust boundary. For example, the agent must not be able to handle certain kinds of data (credit card/account numbers, PII, financial data). A2UI helps enforce the trust boundary and protect your app's critical functionality from hallucinations using a strict schema, and by expressing UI using validated data rather than executable code.

A2UI core philosophy

We develop A2UI under the guidance of the following core principles:

  • Security first: The app developer controls what the agent can and cannot do in the app. A2UI provides a framework for specifying and enforcing the necessary guardrails, such as expressing UI as data, validating inputs and outputs against a schema, and disallowing arbitrary executable code. Every capability granted to the agent is either a safe standard capability built into the framework, or a capability explicitly granted by the app developer.
  • Model-friendly and server-driven: The A2UI protocol is designed to be efficiently generated by language and decision models and transported over the network, and to support progressive rendering (or "streaming") for a responsive user experience. An agent can adapt the UI based on where the user takes the conversation. A2UI supports swappable inference formats, so you can tailor inference to specific models and use cases.
  • Native rendering and portability: A2UI renders UI using the framework native to your app, with renderers for many major UI frameworks. No need to change frameworks unless required for other reasons.

Architecture

A2UI's architecture is made of multiple layers spanning the full stack that connects the agent to the application:

  1. Inference: An agent (typically backed by a language or a decision model) instructed by an A2UI skill (created using an A2UI Agent SDK) generates the description of UI and data using an appropriate inference format (e.g. A2UI Express, or a decision tree).
  2. Transport: An A2UI Agent SDK, embedded in a larger agent architecture, parses and validates the model's output, expands macros, and converts the UI to the wire-stable A2UI Transport protocol messages, which are sent to the renderer.
  3. Rendering: A renderer is made of an A2UI Core library (e.g. the @a2ui/web_core npm package, or a2ui_core Dart package), a UI framework adapter (e.g. @a2ui/react React adapter, or a2ui_flutter Flutter adapter), and a widget catalog. The core library parses the incoming messages and creates a framework-agnostic in-memory representation of the UI and data. The framework adapter maps the in-memory representation to concrete framework-specific UI widgets. The widget catalog provides access to the widgets the agent is allowed to compose.

Getting started

Pick the path that matches where you want to start:

Path What you get Time
🍜 Quickstart A full-stack A2UI app with a backend and frontend. Learn A2UI end-to-end and customize to your use case. ~5 min
🎨 A2UI Composer Generate A2UI JSON from a visual editor and paste it into any agent prompt — no install required. ~1 min
🎬 A2UI Theater Step through pre-built A2UI streaming scenarios across Lit, React, and Angular renderers — no install required. ~1 min

Packages

These packages are developed in this repository. Packages marked "Not published yet" can be used from source.

Python

Package Description Version
a2ui-core Protocol messages, data model, data binding, expression evaluation, and catalog validation.
a2ui-agent-sdk Agent SDK: negotiates catalogs, generates prompts and skills, and compiles model output into A2UI.
a2ui-a2a Connects the agent SDK to the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol.
a2ui-adk Connects the agent SDK to the Agent Development Kit (ADK).

TypeScript

Package Description Version
@a2ui/web_core Protocol messages, state management, expressions, and basic catalog shared by renderers and @a2ui/agent.
@a2ui/lit Lit (web components) renderer.
@a2ui/angular Angular renderer.
@a2ui/react React renderer.
@a2ui/markdown-it Markdown rendering with markdown-it and DOMPurify, shared by the web renderers.
@a2ui/agent Agent SDK: negotiates catalogs, generates prompts and skills, and compiles model output into A2UI.
@a2ui/catalog-mcp MCP catalog: calls MCP tools and renders A2UI messages returned in tool results and UI resources.
@a2ui/catalog-vegachart VegaChart catalog: renders Vega and Vega-Lite chart specifications on A2UI surfaces. Not published yet

Dart and Flutter

Package Description Version
a2ui_core Protocol messages, data model, data binding, and expressions for renderers and agents.
a2ui_agent Agent SDK: negotiates catalogs, generates prompts and skills, and compiles model output into A2UI.
a2ui_flutter Flutter renderer.
a2ui_cli Developer tool that generates typesafe component code from a catalog. GitHub Releases

Swift

The Swift libraries are distributed via Swift Package Manager from Package.swift at the root of this repository.

Package Description
A2UISwiftCore, BasicCatalog Message processor, data model, expression evaluation, and basic catalog definitions.
A2UISwiftUI, BasicCatalogSwiftUI SwiftUI renderer and basic catalog views.

Roadmap

  • Protocol v1.1: We are collecting requirements for the next iteration of the A2UI protocol.
  • Inference: Support for decision models (e.g. Jev).
  • Templates: A cross-framework templating engine and a set of standard primitives for rendering reusable rich UI widgets.
  • Sandboxed logic: A way to securely attach logic to A2UI components.
  • Agent SDK: Skill generation, better diagnostics, and integrations with more agent frameworks.
  • Evals: A set of tools for evaluating generated UI quality.
  • MCP Apps: Embedding MCP Apps inside A2UI, and embedding A2UI experiences into MCP Apps.
  • CLI: Schema validation, codegen, local preview, and integration with coding agents.

Contribute

A2UI is an Apache 2.0 licensed project. We believe the future of UI is agentic, and we want to work with you to help build it.

See CONTRIBUTING.md for details on how to get started.

item.description:
The all-in-one local AI studio for your desktop: chat, image and video generation and a coding agent in one free, open source app. Windows and Linux. No Docker, no terminal, no cloud required.

https://locallyuncensored.com

Locally Uncensored

The all-in-one local AI studio for your desktop. Chat, images, video and a coding agent in one app. Install it, pick a model, go.

Free and open source. In local mode everything runs on your own machine. No Docker, no terminal, no config files. The platforms are listed under Download.

Download · Three steps · What is in the box · How it compares · Models · FAQ

Chat that draws your images Images and video in the same window
The coding agent shows the diff first Agent mode does the legwork

Download

Take the latest build from Releases.

Platform File Status
Windows 10 and 11 Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_x64-setup.exe (NSIS, recommended) or Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_x64_en-US.msi Tested every release, signed auto update channel
Linux Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_amd64.AppImage, Locally.Uncensored_3.0.10_amd64.deb or Locally.Uncensored-3.0.10-1.x86_64.rpm Built on every release
macOS 14 or newer, Apple Silicon (Beta) LU_3.0.10_aarch64.dmg Signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Intel Macs are not supported. The app has run on one Mac so far. Voice has been tried by hand in the app on a Mac and works. Computer control is in the Mac app but not fully tested yet on macOS. Remote Access and the automatic update are not confirmed on macOS
Android 7.0 or newer (arm64) LU-3.0.10-Android.apk The phone app. Not in the Play Store yet: install the file from this page. SHA-256 dbd515d81bbc8ab70f21b850424f9f8b57ae88ae24962225beefc4116d139d2f

Some antivirus engines flag unsigned NSIS installers that download other binaries, which is a false positive. The installer is built by GitHub Actions from the public source on master, and the update channel is signed against a public minisign key, so you can verify both: see SECURITY.md.

Code signing for the Windows installers: free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation. SignPath Foundation has accepted the project. The production certificate is not in place yet, and until it is the installers ship unsigned.

Current release: v3.0.10 (November 2026). Every change since 1.0.0 is in CHANGELOG.md.

3.0.10 fixes lost chats from 3.0.8 and 3.0.9. A backup no longer replaces the only complete copy of your chats, a note at launch says when the backup holds chats that are missing from your list, and Settings, Chat Backup has Restore chats from backup. The Android app is back as an APK, with the keyboard staying open in the Create prompt.

3.0.9 brings Liquid's LFM3 models for small machines: 1.7B and 2B, about 1 to 1.7 GB each, for text, pictures and speech, on the LU Engine, on Ollama or as MLX builds on a Mac; the LU Engine moves to llama.cpp b11960 for them. A group chat now sends every speaker the context you picked, can redo one speaker and lets you set who speaks when. A compaction is one quiet line in the chat, and the conversation before it stays one click away. Animate takes an end image and, with MiniMax H3, up to nine reference pictures, and Krea 2, Qwen-Image 2.1 and FLUX.2 take reference pictures for a style, a person or a pose. Local videos run up to 15 seconds without drifting in colour, and a video shows a rough preview while it renders. The trainer learns a style, a concept or a pose next to a character (Beta). "Use this model" on Hugging Face opens the download in LU, and a model from the search comes in a quant that fits your graphics card. A status menu sits in the Mac menu bar and the Windows and Linux tray, and the Linux AppImage starts again on systems without the tray library. What has only run in automated tests is listed under Known limits in the release notes.

3.0.8 makes web search in the chat work again: LU asks five search services in turn and needs no key for any of them. A video made in the chat plays in the chat, and a long one renders in the background while you write on. A picture attached in the chat reaches the image tool, and with two graphics cards chat and ComfyUI can each get their own. The LU Engine plans a model's memory from the file itself and offers a shorter context with one click. AMD cards on Windows get AMD's current ROCm build. New: the chat can read and change LU's settings with a confirmation card, the Model Manager can make a copy of a local model that refuses less, and Settings, Storage puts models, gallery and runtime in one folder of your choice. What has only run in automated tests is listed under Known limits in the CHANGELOG.

3.0.5 was about Create: LTX 2.5, FastH3 and YuE2 run on your own machine, Qwen-Image 2.1 gets a transparent background and its prompt enhancer, Edit, Remove Background and Enhance Image take up to 50 images in one go, and LU Cloud adds Qwen Image 2.1, LTX 2.5, MiniMax H3 and Wan 3.0 Reference. Chat takes any file, each model in a group chat can have its own persona, dropdowns stay inside the window (issue 149), and the speech install works again on Ubuntu 24.04.

3.0.4 fixed the Code agent and the agent in chat on LU Cloud: writing a long file no longer ends the run, "continue" picks up where a run stopped instead of starting over, the agent keeps a plan only when you ask for one, and cloud context is 32K by default and can be set per model. It also fixed the bugs reported on GitHub and Discord since 3.0.3 (issues 144 to 147): MiniMax H3 runs as a video model with sound, Edit takes up to three extra images with Qwen-Image 2.1, a missing encoder or VAE is named and offered as a download instead of ending in "Value not in list", the LoRA stack follows the loras folder, and group chat works with every LU Engine model.

3.0.3 was a hotfix: chats with many images no longer run the app out of memory, Create reads a model's family from the file instead of its name, and the five bugs reported on GitHub since 3.0.2 are fixed (issues 139 to 143).

3.0.2 was a hotfix: the Code tab lost its scrollbar and its input box once a conversation grew taller than the window (issue 138, a regression in 3.0.1) and is held to the window height again, and the count of open cloud models now takes the Create Studio endpoints in, which makes it fourteen video models and seven image models.

What is new in 3.0.1

  • Qwen-Image 2.1 runs locally on Windows and Linux. One model generates a picture from a prompt and edits one from a reference image, with no mask to paint. About 16 GB of files, ComfyUI 0.37.0 or newer, and a research license that does not allow commercial use.
  • Models has a LoRAs tab of its own. Search CivitAI, download into ComfyUI's models/loras folder, see what is installed with its size and trigger word, and delete what you no longer want.
  • A GPU whose free memory could not be measured is planned more carefully, and the log now says total capacity instead of calling it free.
  • The Linux AppImage stops handing its own runtime to every program LU starts, so a healthy system Python, pip, git or ffmpeg keeps working, and a distribution that blocks pip in the system Python keeps the isolated environment LU built.
  • The local model runs one conversation at a time and says so, with a line showing how many chats are ahead. Stop works while a chat is still waiting.
  • Temperature, Top P and Max tokens belong to the conversation you moved them in, instead of every open chat sharing one value.
  • Cloud video renders offer the clip lengths the picked model really supports, read from the live catalog.

Mobile app (Android, iPhone)

LU is also available as an app for your phone. The current APK comes from the 3.0.10 release.

  • Android: download LU-3.0.10-Android.apk from the 3.0.10 release. Needs Android 7.0 or newer on a 64-bit (arm64) phone. Allow installing apps from your browser or file app when Android asks. SHA-256: dbd515d81bbc8ab70f21b850424f9f8b57ae88ae24962225beefc4116d139d2f
  • iPhone: in review at the App Store.
  • Google Play: coming later.

What the app does:

  • Run AI models on your phone and chat offline. Chats with on-device models stay on the phone.
  • Ask questions about your own documents. Memory and personas.
  • Optional LU Cloud with your account: larger hosted chat models, Create (images and video) and dictation.
  • Connect to LU on your own computer over your home Wi-Fi and chat with the models on your PC.

Later APKs install over this one and keep your data. The Google Play version will be signed by Google: to switch to it, export your chats first (Settings, Data) and uninstall the APK.

Three steps

  1. Install. Run the installer like any other program. On first launch a wizard looks for an AI engine that is already running on your machine, and installs one for you with a single click if there is none. It does the same for ComfyUI, which draws the images and video.
  2. Pick a model. The model manager marks which models fit your hardware and downloads them in one click. It works with the engine you already have (Ollama, LM Studio and others) and can link models those tools already store, without copying them. Loading a model in Ollama or LM Studio can be cancelled, and an Ollama model that runs partly on the processor says so.
  3. Create. Chat, Create, Code and Agent are tabs in one window. Type in one, switch to the next, keep the same models.

Walkthrough with screenshots: Getting started guide. New to local AI: the five minute beginner guide.

Build from source, or contribute 
git clone https://github.com/PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored.git
cd locally-uncensored
npm install
npm run dev          # browser dev mode
npm run tauri build  # desktop binary

setup.bat on Windows and setup.sh on Linux and macOS bootstrap Node, Git and Ollama for dev mode. See the contributing guide.

What is in the box

Chat. Models that answer directly, without refusals, next to the mainstream ones in the same menu. Thinking is shown as it happens, with an effort control on the models that offer one. Upload an image and ask about it (a local model with image input is downloaded together with its image part, the second file it needs to see pictures), chat with your own documents through a local index, talk instead of typing and have answers read back, keep a memory across conversations, switch personas, and import your ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini export so the old threads come with you. A long conversation folds its older turns into a summary instead of running out of room.

Create. Images and video on your own GPU through a ComfyUI the app installs, starts, repairs and updates for you. No node graphs. The lanes are text to image, edit and image to image with a mask for inpainting, remove background, video, animate an image, extend a clip, motion control, talking character, music, and Character Studio, which trains a character on your own card and drops it into your local LoRA folder. A LoRA picker with a stack and strength sliders reads the folder live, and everything you make lands in the gallery. Upscale and Erase Object are the two lanes that run in the cloud only. How it works.

Code. A coding agent that builds a map of the repo, edits only the lines you asked for, shows the diff before it applies anything, runs your tests and reads the failures, and carries typed git tools and per project rules in a .lurules file. Ask, Plan and Bypass modes per conversation, a file explorer with preview, and a workspace per project. A Local API in Settings puts every local model on one OpenAI compatible address behind a token, so your other coding tools can use the same machine.

Agent. Web search and fetch, reading and writing files, a shell, code execution, screenshots, image and video generation, and your own MCP servers on top. Long jobs go to background agents that work while you carry on, and a panel shows what is running. Every tool call passes a permission gate you control, and a read only run stays read only.

Voice (Beta). A spoken conversation with the chat model you picked. Speech recognition, the voice and the turn taking run on your own machine, in English, with fifteen voices. You can interrupt an answer by speaking, the model can use the agent tools with the same permissions, and you decide whether those tools reach your workspace folder or the whole computer. Voice runs in local mode only, and with the Cloud switch on it is hidden. Voice is in beta: it is new, and your computer may still show rough edges. Our check in the real app ran on Windows, and on a Mac Voice has been tried by hand in the app. VOICE.md has the setup and what was measured.

Computer control (Beta). A model looks at the screen and uses the mouse and the keyboard in apps you approve. It is off until you switch it on, asks once in every new chat before it starts, asks before every action unless you make a session autonomous, and never touches terminals, password managers or password fields. Anything that sends, buys or deletes needs your click, and so does a button without a name. In an autonomous session, moving the mouse pauses it, and a shortcut stops it at any time. It is in beta: it is new and not proven in every app yet, so watch what it does and stop it when it goes wrong. Our check in the real app ran on Windows. On a Mac it is in the app but not fully tested yet. COMPUTER-CONTROL.md lists what it asks and what it never touches.

Everywhere. Reach the app from your phone over your LAN or through a Cloudflare tunnel, paired by QR code and a passcode, off until you turn it on, with connected devices listed. Compare two models side by side, benchmark them on your own hardware for speed, cost and correctness, and take updates over a signed channel. Phone details.

Optional: LU Labs Cloud

Some models are larger than any desktop card. Flip the Cloud switch in the same app and those run on hosted GPUs instead, with the heavy Create lanes alongside them. The same account works in the browser at lu-labs.ai, on a plan or on credit packs that do not expire. The local app stays free either way, and switching back to local costs nothing: plans and prices. With Create in chat (Beta), a cloud chat model can put together an order for images, video, music or voice, and nothing runs until you approve it.

Since 3.0.0 the catalogue says what it can back up. Every cloud chat model was asked the same two questions twice and judged on the answer, and a longer three-round test on 2026-10-05 took the mark from five more: 19 of the 46 we measured answer in full, and only those carry the No Filter mark in the picker. Across all measured answers, 5% were refusals. Ten more chat models that their makers release to answer without refusing are listed as a group of their own, marked Uncensored (Beta). They were not part of the measurement above. On an active plan, 11 models on Hosted and 12 on Pro and Max cost no credits in chat, up to a daily limit. For images and video, 14 video and 7 image models run without a built-in content restriction, most of them with Uncensored in the name, and your account decides what they may produce.

How it compares

Locally Uncensored Open WebUI LM Studio Jan SillyTavern
Chat Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes
Image generation Yes No No No Partial
Video generation Yes No No No No
Image to image and image to video Yes No No No No
Coding agent Yes No No No No
Agent with tools and MCP Yes No No No No
Works out of the box Yes No Yes Yes No
Remote access from your phone Yes Partial No No Partial
Compare and benchmark Yes No No No No
Answers directly, without refusals Yes No No No Partial
Voice in and out Yes Partial No No Partial
Document chat Yes Yes No No No
Runs without Docker Yes No Yes Yes Yes
Open source Yes Yes No Yes Yes

Deep dives: vs LM Studio · vs Jan · vs Open WebUI · vs GPT4All · vs Msty · vs KoboldCpp · vs SillyTavern · LM Studio alternatives · Best local AI apps 2026

Models that run well

The model manager holds the full catalog and marks what fits your machine. These are the ones worth starting with.

Text

Music runs on ACE Step 1.5 Turbo at 6-8 GB, and Talking Character on Wan 2.2 S2V from 10-12 GB.

Bring your own engine

If you already run a local engine, the app finds it and lists it instead of installing a second one. It detects twelve of them: Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, GPT4All, KoboldCpp, llama.cpp, vLLM, LocalAI, text-generation-webui, TabbyAPI, Aphrodite and SGLang. It also ships its own LU Engine for people who have none. Cloud providers are optional and use your own keys: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, DeepSeek, Mistral, or any OpenAI compatible address you paste in.

FAQ

Is it really free and offline? Yes. AGPL-3.0, no account, no usage limits. In local mode chat, agent runs and image and video generation all happen on your machine, and after the model download they work without a connection. The app has no analytics kit and sends no crash reports. On its own it uses the network for two things: it checks GitHub Releases for updates shortly after start and at most every six hours after that, and it counts each press of the Cloud switch (which way, platform, app version, no identifier). While you are signed in to LU Cloud it also checks your account every five minutes. Settings, General, Privacy has the full list.

What does "uncensored" mean? Abliterated models have the trained in refusal behaviour removed from the weights, so it is not a jailbreak that can be patched or break. They answer directly, without refusals. Full guide.

What hardware do I need? Chat runs a 3B model on 8 GB of system RAM with no GPU at all, and an 8B model comfortably on a 6 GB card. Image generation starts at 6 to 8 GB of VRAM, and so does video on AnimateDiff Lightning or FramePack F1; the Wan and Hunyuan models want 12 GB or more. The model manager marks what fits before you download. Chat runs on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel cards through the Vulkan build of the LU Engine on Windows and Linux. Images and video run on NVIDIA, on AMD with ROCm on Linux (RX 6800 and newer, RX 7000, RX 9000) and, from 3.0.8, on Windows for RX 7000 and RX 9000.

Can I run it on a Linux server, without a screen? LU is a desktop app with a window, so it needs a graphical session: a desktop on the server, or one you reach over VNC or RDP. There is no --host flag. For other machines on your network, Settings, Voice & Remote, Local API with "Reachable on the network" gives every running local model an OpenAI compatible address on port 8129 (it binds all interfaces, needs a token, and serves the models that are loaded in LU, Ollama or LM Studio). "Start with LU" (3.0.8) brings it up on every launch. The full chat and agent window from another device is the Remote tab with LAN, on port 11435. On a server without a Vulkan driver the LU Engine runs on the processor; install mesa-vulkan-drivers (Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora) or vulkan-radeon (Arch) for an AMD card, and the app says so when it happens.

Can it replace ChatGPT or Claude? For most chat, writing and coding, yes, with a good 8B to 14B local model, and it stays private and unlimited. Frontier cloud models are still stronger on the hardest reasoning. You can add them with your own API keys, or use the Cloud switch.

Does remote access leak data? Remote access is off until you start it, sits behind a six-digit passcode, and shows when a device is connected. On your own network the chat goes straight from phone to PC. Over the internet Cloudflare relays it: the traffic is encrypted to and from Cloudflare, not end to end, so Cloudflare could read it.

What about macOS? The macOS row of the Download table says whether the current release has a Mac build. On a Mac, chat runs on local models through the bundled server with Metal, and Create makes images and video on the Mac itself, without ComfyUI, so what this README says about ComfyUI, VRAM and LoRA folders describes Windows and Linux. On any Mac you can use LU Cloud in the browser at lu-labs.ai, which runs chat, images and video on hosted GPUs.

Roadmap

Updated 5 November 2026. Everything up to 3.0.10 has shipped; Releases has the history.

Just out: 3.0.10

  • Lost chats from 3.0.8 and 3.0.9: a note at launch when the backup still holds them, and Restore chats from backup in Settings
  • The Android app as an APK again, with the keyboard staying open in the Create prompt

3.0.9

  • Liquid LFM3 for small machines: text, pictures and speech, with llama.cpp b11960 in the LU Engine
  • Group chat with the full context you picked, one speaker redone at a time, and a speaking order
  • Animate with an end image and reference pictures, reference pictures in Create

item.title: shanliuling/dsh-image-gen
item.description:
可在对话内生成、编辑、对比图像；内置 500 + 提示词、图库、多模型工作流，支持 ComfyUI。AI image studio for DeepSeek Harness — generate, edit & compare images in chat, with 500+ prompts, gallery, multi-model workflows and ComfyUI.

https://github.com/shanliuling/dsh-image-gen#readme


简体中文 · English

🎨 dsh-image-gen

在 DeepSeek Harness 里，用说话的方式画图

对话批量生图 · GIF 动图 · 看得懂草图的 AI 画布 · Agent 自动套用 500+ Prompt 灵感 · 订阅账号免 Key

一句话就能做到 · 快速开始 · 核心能力 · Provider 支持 · 常见问题


🔁 一句话，一整组图
一条消息Agent 批量生成几十张图片		 ✏️ 画个草图、圈个地方，AI 就懂
圈出剑 → 换成斧头 · 火柴人 → 成图

dsh-image-gen 是 DeepSeek Harness 的原生图像创作插件。它不是在对话框里塞一个生图按钮，而是让 Agent 本身学会画图：它能一次规划并生成一整组图，能看懂你在画布上的涂鸦和圈选，能自己去灵感库里找合适的风格模板。需要精细控制时，还有 Studio 工作台、多模型对比和图库。

已有 ChatGPT、Grok 或 Google 订阅？直接登录即可生图，无需额外购买 API Key。

支持：Gemini · OpenAI / Compatible · Seedream · DashScope · Grok Imagine · GLM-Image · 本地 ComfyUI

pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-image-gen@latest

每个版本的更新内容见 Releases。

一句话就能做到

不用学参数，也不用切页面，直接在 DSH 对话里说：

你在对话里说 插件会做什么
「给《咖啡店开业》这篇文章配 4 张插图，统一扁平插画风，16:9」 🔁 对话批量生图：Agent 把需求拆成 4 个 Prompt 逐张生成，一条消息收齐整组图
「用手绘风格 #123 画一张咖啡店菜单」 ✨ 自动套用灵感：Agent 先在 500+ 案例库里检索对应风格，再套用模板出图
「把我在画布上画的草图变成正式插画」 ✏️ 看懂画布：Agent 读取画布选区，把草稿变成成图
「把我圈出来的剑换成斧头，其他不变」 🎯 圈哪改哪：只改你标出的局部
「保持这个角色不变，换到雪地场景」 🎭 角色一致性：图生图时保持同一个人物或物体，不会换成长得相似的另一个
「同一个 Prompt，GPT 和 Gemini 各出一张对比」 ⚖️ 多模型对比：并发调用多个模型，放在同一张画布上比较
「把这个角色做成一段挥手的 GIF 动图」 🎞️ GIF 动图：直接生成循环动画，卡片里播放、调倍速，还能按帧写评论修改

快速开始

加固下载（可选）

两条可选设置加固离开本机的网络路径，默认全部关闭：

  • strictImageDownloads：结果 URL 必须是公网 HTTPS 443。DNS 解析结果会校验并固定用于本次请求，不跟随 provider 结果中的重定向，响应遵守图片字节上限。
  • requireHostAdmission：宿主 connection admission 服务缺失或异常时，插件 Web 路由一律 503 拒绝，而不是裸奔。

默认关闭是因为 TUN 代理或自定义企业解析器可能故意返回内网地址；开启任一设置即假定你的出口是直连。

1. 安装插件

环境要求：DeepSeek Harness 稳定版本，Node.js ^22.19.0 或 >= 24.0.0。

在你的 DeepSeek Harness 项目根目录下运行：

pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-image-gen@latest

💬 极客提示：你也可以直接把这句话发送给 DSH 对话中的 Agent：
帮我安装生图插件，在终端执行：pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-image-gen@latest

其他安装方式（全局 / GitHub 直装 / 本地调试） 
# 若已将 dsh 安装为系统全局命令：
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-image-gen@latest

# 从 GitHub 仓库直接安装最新代码：
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/shanliuling/dsh-image-gen.git

# 本地克隆源码开发安装：
git clone https://github.com/shanliuling/dsh-image-gen.git
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-image-gen

2. 配置 Provider

重启 DSH 后，点击左侧边栏的 「插件」 图标打开插件面板，在 「已安装」 分区点击 dsh-image-gen，进入插件详情页即可看到「图像生成」配置表单：

插件面板 → 已安装 → dsh-image-gen

DSH 0.1.5 及更早版本没有插件面板，入口仍为「设置 → 插件 → 插件配置 → 图像生成」；插件已同时兼容两种入口。

选择 Provider，填写自己的 API Key，并按需调整模型、Endpoint / Base URL 与工作区保存选项。填好 Key 后可点击「测试连接」验证可用性，或点击「拉取模型」一键获取该厂商支持的全部生图模型，无需手动查文档。使用 ComfyUI 时，请填写 DSH Host 可访问的服务地址，并导入 API Format Workflow JSON；导入多个工作流后，可在对话输入框旁的生图按钮里直接切换。

已有 ChatGPT、Grok 或 Google 订阅？无需填写 API Key：展开对应的订阅 Provider 行，点击「登录」并在浏览器完成授权，即可直接开始文生图与图生图。


选默认 Provider → 查看各渠道的 Key / 登录状态 → 在对话输入框旁随手切换。

3. 开始创作

在聊天框中直接描述你想要的图片：

画一张雨夜霓虹街头的赛博朋克猫咪，电影感光线，16:9。

想要一整组图？直接说数量和统一风格：

给我的小红书笔记《周末露营清单》配 5 张图：帐篷、炉具、睡袋、照明、零食，统一日系手绘风，3:4。

也可以直接上传参考图，让 Agent 进行风格重构或局部编辑：

保持角色与构图不变，给猫咪戴上一副黑色墨镜。


在对话中直接生图、图生图与连续编辑。

需要更细的参数控制时，点击会话顶部的 画廊 入口，进入 图库 / 工作台 / 灵感 / 收藏。

核心能力

🔁 对话批量生图：一句话，一整组图

配图、分镜、系列插画、同一主题的多个变体，不用一张一张地催。

  • 用一句话描述数量和统一要求，Agent 会自己规划出一组 Prompt，单次最多 10 张，图片按顺序附在同一条回复里。
  • 比例、清晰度、模型、Provider 可以对整组统一指定，保证风格一致。
  • 逐张生成，某一张失败不会影响其余图片，最后会汇报「成功 X / 共 Y」并列出失败原因。
  • 本地 ComfyUI 和订阅通道同样支持批量。

一条消息写 5 个画面 → Agent 规划成两批生成 → 逐张出图，失败的那张自动单独重跑 → 整组进入图库。（等待部分已加速）

对话批量和 Studio 批量有什么区别？ 对话批量是 Agent 帮你规划一组不同的画面（例如 4 张不同场景的插图）；Studio 批量是同一个 Prompt 出多张候选，由你挑选满意的保存。


✏️ 看得懂草图的 AI 画布

在无限画布上画草图、摆参考图、圈出要改的地方，然后直接用对话告诉 AI 你想要什么。Agent 能看到画布上的内容和你当前的选区，不需要你截图、上传或者描述位置。

  • 草图 → 成图：随手画个轮廓，选中它说「画成卡通角色」。
  • 圈哪改哪：在已有图片上用画笔圈出局部，说「把这里换成斧头」，只改圈出的部分。
  • 组合参考：把「最近生成」或图库里的图拖进画布，或点击缩略图上的「发送到画布」，多张一起选中作为参考。同一张历史图片重复导入会自动去重。
  • 每一步结果都留在画布上，随时可以从任意一版继续往下迭代。

圈哪改哪：圈出女剑士手里的剑，说「变成一把斧头」，Agent 先确认圈的是什么，再只改那一处。


草图 → 成图：随手画个持剑的火柴人，框选后说「按照之前风格生成」，姿势和构图都照着草图来。（等待部分已加速）

💬 对话生图、编辑与版本切换

  • 用自然语言完成文生图、图生图、多图参考和风格迁移。
  • 角色一致性：要求「保持这个人物 / 角色 / 物体不变」时，插件会让模型沿用参考图里的同一主体，只改场景、服装、姿势或风格，而不是重新画一个相似的人。
  • 直接修改原图 Prompt 重新生成，并在同一卡片中切换历史版本。


修改 Prompt 后原位重新生成，并在同一张图片卡片中切换历史版本。

🎞️ GIF 动图：生成、播放、按帧修改

使用 GPT Image 2.6 等支持动图的模型时，直接在对话里说「做成 GIF / 动图」即可得到循环动画，也可以把参考图里的角色做成动图。帧数与帧时长可用 frame_count（2–16）、frame_duration_ms（20–2000 ms）指定。

  • 生成结果是 GIF 时，对话卡片直接播放动画：左下角调倍速（0.2×–2×），工具栏的下载菜单可按当前倍速或原速下载 GIF、或下载当前帧（PNG）；点开大图有播放键、逐帧缩略图时间轴（悬停预览、点击停在这一帧）和倍速。图库里的 GIF 带角标、悬停即播放，大图同样可播放与下载。GIF 文件可直接拖出，重新生成仍得到 GIF（剪贴板只支持静态图，复制得到的是单帧）。
  • GIF 卡片右下角「编辑」（或大图播放条的「编辑帧」）可按帧写修改意见：在画面上点位置写评论，评论只显示在它所在的那一帧，也可切到「全部帧」一次看全；一次发送即按评论重绘整段，新结果作为新版本保留并会动（仅 OpenAI 与兼容渠道，且中转需支持图生图；不支持时可一键改为描述后重新生成）。
  • 支持渠道：OpenAI 官方与 OpenAI 兼容中转（需模型与中转支持 GIF）。ChatGPT 订阅使用的 Codex 图片接口目前上游未开放 GIF，暂不支持。

🖼️ SVG 矢量输出

生图时也可以要求矢量结果：generate_image 传 output_format: "svg"（仅 OpenAI 官方与兼容中转的文生图；图生图接口不支持 SVG）。

  • 结果会进入对话图卡：卡片直接显示矢量图（点开可放大，无损），工具栏可复制 SVG 源码、下载 .svg、在侧栏打开保存的文件。DSH 附件层只保存 png/jpeg/webp/gif，所以卡片是用工具结果里的 SVG 源码渲染的，图库与版本历史仍只收录位图。
  • SVG 没有像素尺寸，size / aspect_ratio / image_size 不会发送，结果里会给出一条说明；frame_count / frame_duration_ms 只属于 GIF，与 SVG 一起传会直接报错。

✨ 500+ Prompt 灵感：Agent 会自己去找

内置手绘风格手册（风格 / 排版 / 单色主题色）和 awesome-gpt-image-2 案例集，共 500+ 个可直接复用的 Prompt。

  • 在对话里直接点名：说「用风格 #123」「做成信息图排版」「莫兰迪色系」，Agent 会先在灵感库里检索，再把模板套到你的主题上出图。风格、排版、主题色还可以组合使用。
  • 在界面里浏览：筛选、收藏、复制，或一键带入工作台（见下方 Studio 演示）。
  • 图片缓存在本地，浏览和学习不消耗 Token 或生成额度。


先找灵感，再把 Prompt 带入工作台；全本地缓存，浏览或复制不消耗生成额度。

🎛️ Studio 工作台：不用对话，自己调参数

想精细控制时，打开会话顶部的 画廊 → 工作台，所有参数都摆在面前。

  • 从灵感直接开工：在灵感库里点「带入工作台」，Prompt 自动填好。
  • 参数一目了然：Provider、模型、比例、生成质量、水印都能单独选；一次出 1–4 张候选，满意的才保存。
  • 拿历史结果继续改：从「最近生成」拖一张图进来，点「继续编辑（垫图）」，它就自动成为图生图的参考图（最多 5 张）。
  • 单模型 / 多模型对比一键切换。


灵感库挑一个 Prompt → 带入工作台 → 选好参数开始生成 → 出图后再决定保存。（等待部分已加速）


从「最近生成」拖一张图进来 → 「继续编辑（垫图）」→ 自动切到图生图，写一句要改什么就行。

⚖️ 多模型横向对比

使用同一组 Prompt 和参考图并发调用多个模型，在一张画布中比较并保存结果。



在同一画布中比较不同模型结果，再批量保存满意的图片。

🖼️ 图库、收藏与批量管理

  • 统一管理对话和 Studio 中保存的图片，并按工作区隔离。
  • 支持搜索、筛选、收藏、下载、继续编辑、重新生成和批量管理。


图库支持多维度筛选、收藏、批量管理与工作区数据隔离。

🧩 本地 ComfyUI 多工作流

灵活调用本地 GPU 算力，让私有化绘图无缝融入 Agent 对话。

  • 导入并管理多个命名工作流，支持预设 Prompt 和常用占位符。
  • Agent 可按名称选择工作流，在对话中完成文生图、图生图和批量生图。
  • 占位符：{{prompt}}、{{seed}}；宽高写 {{width}}/{{height}} 后，Agent 传入的尺寸或比例才会生效（默认 1024×1024）；图生图在 LoadImage 写 {{image}}，多张参考图就写多个，按节点编号顺序对应。

ComfyUI 暂未接入 Studio 和多模型对比。



为不同用途维护独立工作流，并通过名称让 Agent 精确选择。

Provider 支持情况

Provider 对话生图 对话批量 对话编辑 Studio 多模型对比 GIF
Google Gemini ✅ ✅ ✅ 多图 ✅ ✅ —
OpenAI Images ✅ ✅ ✅ 多图 ✅ ✅ ✅
OpenAI Compatible（中转站） ✅ ✅ ✅ 多图 ✅ ✅ ✅
ByteDance Seedream / 火山方舟 ✅ ✅ ✅ 多图 ✅ ✅ —
Aliyun DashScope / Qwen Image ✅ ✅ ✅ 多图 ✅ ✅ —
xAI Grok Imagine ✅ ✅ ⚠️ 有限 ✅ ✅ —
智谱 GLM-Image ✅ ✅ — ✅ ✅ —
Local ComfyUI ✅ ✅ ✅ 多图 — — —
ChatGPT 订阅（免 Key） ✅ ✅ ✅ 多图 ✅ ✅ —
Grok 订阅（免 Key） ✅ ✅ ✅ 多图 ✅ ✅ —
Google 订阅（免 Key） ✅ ✅ ✅ 多图 ✅ ✅ —

Studio 与多模型对比目前只支持云端 Provider（含订阅通道）；多模型对比调用的是各 Provider 在设置中已配置的模型。 智谱 GLM-Image 上游本身不支持图生图；xAI 图生图走 OpenAI 兼容协议（multipart），部分网关可能需等待后续适配。 订阅通道通过账号登录使用（免 API Key），图生图走各订阅渠道的编辑接口（最多 5 张参考图），比例与清晰度可在 Studio 中直接选择。 OpenAI 与兼容渠道的对话生图和图生图都可以直接要求输出 GIF 动图，例如把参考图里的角色做成动图（需模型与中转支持；图生图还要求中转支持改图接口），帧数、帧时长等参数见 Provider 配置参考。ChatGPT 订阅使用的接口暂不支持 GIF 输出。

📖 默认模型与 Endpoint、各 Provider 的比例 / 清晰度、尺寸表、水印、中转站编辑格式等高级配置，见 Provider 配置参考。

数据与隐私

  • BYOK：API Key 通过 DSH Credentials 服务保存，设置页不会回显 Key 明文。
  • 订阅登录：订阅账号令牌经你授权登录后保存于 DSH Credentials，与 API Key 完全隔离，浏览器侧不接触令牌。
  • 云端请求：Prompt 与本次使用的参考图会发送给所选 Provider，请遵守对应服务条款。
  • 上游图片下载：沿用宿主已有的网络和代理配置，不额外拦截 Fake-IP、内网或回环地址。当前未提供完整的 SSRF 目标限制。
  • 本地 ComfyUI：请求发送到用户配置的 ComfyUI 地址。
  • 工作区文件：开启工作区保存后，对话结果会落盘；Studio 仅保存用户选中的候选图。
  • GIF 原图：动图结果的原始文件另存于原图保险库（vaultEnabled 可关闭），供卡片播放与导出，随图库删除一并清理。
  • 图库与收藏：图库元数据和收藏状态保存在当前浏览器本地存储中。
  • 删除记录：普通删除会保留轻量的图片 ID 标记，超过 30 天也不会因重新打开旧会话而自动恢复到图库。
  • 灵感缓存：案例元数据随插件提供，图片按需加载并缓存在本机，可随时清理。

常见问题

安装后找不到“图像生成”设置怎么办？

设置入口随 DSH 版本不同：0.1.6 及以上位于插件详情页（点击左侧边栏「插件」图标，在「已安装」分区进入 dsh-image-gen），0.1.5 及更早位于「设置 → 插件 → 插件配置 → 图像生成」。

若两处都没有，先完全重启当前 DSH Profile，再检查插件配置：

dsh --profile web --dump-config

如果输出中没有 dsh-image-gen，请重新执行安装命令。提交 Issue 时请附 DSH 版本、插件版本和错误日志，不要上传 API Key。

一次最多能批量生成多少张？

对话批量单次调用最多 10 张，超过时插件会提示 Agent 拆成多次调用。图片是逐张生成的，单张失败不会中断其余图片，失败的会在结果里单独列出原因。

生成图片保存在哪里？

开启“保存到工作区”后，对话生成结果默认保存在当前工作区的 dsh-image-gen/ 子目录，也可以在设置中修改。Studio 候选图先留在临时画布，只有用户选中的结果才会进入图库并保存。

Gemini 中转只支持 generateContent，如何配置？

在 Google Gemini 设置中，将“请求协议”改为“原生 generateContent”，接口地址填写中转的 API 基础地址，例如 https://your-relay.example/v1beta，保存后即可用于对话生图、图生图和 Studio。已有的 Interactions 完整地址也可以沿用，插件会按所选模型构建原生请求地址。

配置文件对应 googleNative: true；默认值为 false，现有用户仍使用 Interactions 协议。

为什么 ComfyUI 没有出现在 Studio 中？

当前 Studio 与多模型对比仅支持云端 Provider，暂未接入 ComfyUI。ComfyUI 已支持在 Agent 对话中进行文生图、图生图（支持多张参考图）、批量生图以及多个命名工作流。

从图库删除会删除聊天记录吗？

不会。删除图库记录不会修改原聊天消息。你可以额外选择是否清理工作区中的本地图片文件；文件删除通常无法恢复，请确认后操作。

如何升级？ 
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-image-gen@latest

升级后重启对应的 DSH Profile。

本地开发

git clone https://github.com/shanliuling/dsh-image-gen.git
cd dsh-image-gen

pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm run build
pnpm run pack:check
pnpm run test:package

依赖要求与 test:package 的测试范围等维护者说明见 CONTRIBUTING.md。欢迎通过 Issues 反馈问题，或阅读贡献指南后提交 Pull Request。

item.title: EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
item.description:
Official Compound Engineering plugin for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more

https://every.to/compound-engineering

Compound Engineering

AI skills that make each unit of engineering work easier than the last.

Compound Engineering is a plugin of 38 skills for AI coding agents. It structures the work around a loop — brainstorm, plan, build, review, then capture what you learned — so the knowledge from each change is written down where the next change can read it.

It runs on 14 agent hosts, including Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

Maintained by Kieran Klaassen and Trevin Chow, with contributions from the open-source community.

For understanding before a change, ask ce-explain how the relevant behavior works and why it exists. For a recommendation, use ce-pov; “oracle this” adds independent model opinions. Both can contribute to another workflow without a separate human interaction.

Install

Claude Code

/plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
/plugin install compound-engineering

Important

Already have Compound Engineering installed? Refresh the marketplace before updating — see Upgrading. Running /plugin update alone keeps you on the old version.

Cursor

In Cursor Agent chat, install from the plugin marketplace:

/add-plugin compound-engineering

Or search for "compound engineering" in the plugin marketplace.

Grok Bot

Grok Bot is its own app, but it uses your Cursor account and plugin library. There is no separate Grok Bot login. Install Compound Engineering once on that account and Grok Bot agents can load it.

In Cursor Agent chat:

/add-plugin compound-engineering

Or search for "compound engineering" in the Cursor plugin marketplace. Do not run /add-plugin in the Grok Bot chat, and do not clone this repository onto the Grok Bot computer.

Codex App

Compound Engineering is not listed in Codex's built-in plugin marketplace yet. Add it as a custom marketplace:

  1. In the Codex app, open Plugins from the sidebar.

  2. Click the arrow next to Create, then select Add marketplace.

  3. Enter:

    Field Value
    Source EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
    Git ref main
    Sparse paths leave blank

  4. Click Add marketplace.

  5. Search for Compound Engineering, install compound-engineering-plugin, then restart Codex.

The Codex app install is self-contained for Compound Engineering. Specialist reviewer and research behavior lives inside the skills as local prompt assets; no separate custom-agent install step is required.

Codex CLI

Register the marketplace, then install the plugin.

  1. Register the marketplace with Codex:

    codex plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin

  2. Install the plugin:

    codex plugin add compound-engineering@compound-engineering-plugin

    You can also launch codex, run /plugins, find the Compound Engineering marketplace, select the compound-engineering plugin, and choose Install. Restart Codex after install completes.

The native Codex plugin install is self-contained for Compound Engineering. Specialist reviewer and research behavior lives inside the skills as local prompt assets; no separate custom-agent install step is required.

For a non-default Codex profile, run every Codex-related step against the same CODEX_HOME. This example installs CE into a work profile:

CODEX_HOME="$HOME/.codex/profiles/work" codex plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
CODEX_HOME="$HOME/.codex/profiles/work" codex plugin add compound-engineering@compound-engineering-plugin

The marketplace step only makes the plugin available; the plugin install is what activates the native CE skills for that profile.

Another editor or CLI? Kimi Code CLI, Cline, Grok Build CLI, Devin CLI, GitHub Copilot, Factory Droid, Qwen Code, OpenCode, Pi, oh-my-pi (omp), and Antigravity CLI are all supported — see More install options.

Philosophy

Each unit of engineering work should make subsequent units easier -- not harder.

Invocation syntax: this README uses /skill-name examples for slash-skill hosts. In Codex, invoke installed skills with $skill-name (for example, $ce-plan and $lfg). In oh-my-pi (omp), these prompts can model-route to visible skills; use the native deterministic /skill:<name> form for manual-only or hidden skills (for example, /skill:ce-polish). /goal remains a Codex built-in command.

Traditional development accumulates technical debt. Every feature adds complexity. Every bug fix leaves behind a little more local knowledge that someone has to rediscover later. The codebase gets larger, the context gets harder to hold, and the next change becomes slower.

Compound engineering inverts this. 80% is in planning and review, 20% is in execution:

  • Plan thoroughly before writing code with /ce-brainstorm and /ce-plan using one plan artifact that grows from requirements into implementation planning
  • Review to catch issues and calibrate judgment with /ce-code-review and /ce-doc-review
  • Codify knowledge so it is reusable with /ce-compound
  • Keep quality high so future changes are easy

The point is leverage, not ceremony. A good brainstorm makes the plan sharper. A good plan makes execution smaller. A good review catches the pattern, not just the bug. A good compound note means the next agent does not have to learn the same lesson from scratch.

The loop

The core loop is six steps: brainstorm the requirements, plan the implementation, work through the plan, simplify what you wrote, review the result, then compound the learning -- and repeat with better context.

Skill Purpose
/ce-brainstorm Interactive Q&A to think through a feature or problem and write a requirements-only unified plan before planning
/ce-plan Enrich feature ideas or requirements-only plans into implementation-ready plans
/ce-work Execute implementation-ready plans natively or through a qualified cross-model author while retaining host verification, commits, and shipping
/ce-simplify-code Refine the freshly written code and prune useless tests and comments before review
/ce-code-review Report-only multi-agent review against the plan before merging; local apply is explicit
/ce-compound Capture the learning into docs/solutions/ so the next loop starts smarter

Each cycle compounds. /ce-compound writes learnings that the next /ce-brainstorm and /ce-plan read as grounding. Brainstorms sharpen plans, plans inform future plans, reviews catch more issues, patterns get documented. That return arrow is the whole point.

Run one teaches it. Run two remembers.

Replayed from a real pair of sessions 18 days apart, with names and paths anonymized and the six-minute run compressed to about 30 seconds. Nothing shown is behavior the skills don't have — see assets/demo for the source and the substitutions.

Artifact folders like docs/solutions/ and docs/plans/ are the defaults. A project whose docs/ is tracked content can relocate every CE artifact folder under one repo-relative root via the docs_root setting -- see configuration.

Want the same knowledge compounding across every repo in your org -- team conventions, security policies, a stack's hard-won rules -- instead of being relearned in each one? Declare it as Compound Packs: folders of prescriptive rules (local, or ref-pinned git repos) that planning grounds in and review enforces, every use cited back to the rule file (experimental) -- see Compound Packs.

Try it

After installing, run /ce-setup in any project. It reports optional tool capabilities, creates repo .compound-engineering/config.yaml when missing, refreshes the committed example, and gitignores an existing local override. Not sure which skill to run, or what comes next? Ask /ce-help.

The standard loop -- turn a rough idea into shipped, reviewed code:

/ce-brainstorm make background job retries safer
/ce-plan
/ce-work
/ce-simplify-code
/ce-code-review
/ce-compound

Autonomous -- hand off a feature and let the agent run the whole pipeline:

/ce-brainstorm describe the feature
/lfg

/lfg runs the loop hands-off: it picks the route to a verified work source (a plan, or a ce-debug fix for a bug report), works through it, simplifies, runs code review and applies the fixes, captures any durable learning, runs browser tests, then commits. When a git remote exists it pushes, opens a PR, and watches CI with a bounded repair loop (it does not merge unless you grant that, and it can finish with leftovers if the repair budget is hit). With no remote it stops at local commits. Start it after /ce-brainstorm so it plans against real requirements rather than a one-line prompt.

Starting from a bug instead of a feature? Use /ce-debug. Not sure what to build yet? Start with /ce-ideate.

Skills at a glance

38 skills, grouped by what they are for. The full catalog, with a page per skill and how each one chains into the others, is in docs/guides.

Group Skills What it covers
Core loop ce-brainstorm ce-plan ce-work ce-simplify-code ce-code-review ce-compound The six steps of every iteration
Around the loop ce-strategy ce-product-pulse ce-sweep ce-retro ce-compound-refresh Anchors and feeds that keep the loop grounded
On demand ce-ideate ce-bakeoff ce-pov ce-debug ce-explain ce-doc-review ce-optimize ce-prototype Reached for when a specific need arises
Git workflow ce-commit ce-commit-push-pr ce-babysit-pr ce-resolve-pr-feedback ce-worktree Committing, shipping, and shepherding PRs
Autonomous lfg The whole pipeline, hands-off
Testing & design ce-test-browser ce-test-xcode ce-polish ce-dogfood Verifying and polishing what you built
Collaboration ce-proof ce-handoff ce-promote Sharing work and handing it off
Utilities ce-help ce-setup ce-noslop wtf ce-retune ce-riffrec-feedback-analysis Help, setup, writing, and maintenance

Learn more

  • Skill documentation catalog
  • Compound engineering: how Every codes with agents
  • The story behind compounding engineering

More Install Options

Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex are at the top. Everything here is equally supported.

Kimi Code CLI

Kimi Code CLI can install Compound Engineering directly from this repository because the repo ships a native .kimi-plugin/plugin.json manifest:

/plugins install https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin

You can also browse it through Kimi's custom marketplace flow:

/plugins marketplace https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin/main/.kimi-plugin/marketplace.json

After installing or updating, run /reload or start a new Kimi session so the plugin skills are loaded.

Cline

Cline loads CE skills from on-demand SKILL.md directories. Enable Settings -> Features -> Enable Skills in the Cline extension, then link this repository's skills globally or per project:

git clone https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
./compound-engineering-plugin/.cline/scripts/install-skills.sh --global

Per-project install from a checkout:

./compound-engineering-plugin/.cline/scripts/install-skills.sh --project

Start a new Cline task after installing or updating skills. See .cline/INSTALL.md for pinning, local development, and uninstall steps.

Grok Build CLI (grok)

xAI's Grok Build CLI (grok) installs Compound Engineering directly from this repository. The repo root is a valid Grok plugin: grok reads the existing Claude-compatible manifests, and the repo also ships a native .grok-plugin/plugin.json.

grok plugin install EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin

This tracks the repository; run grok plugin update to pull the latest. To browse it as a marketplace source instead, the repo ships a native .grok-plugin/marketplace.json:

grok plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
grok plugin install compound-engineering

Both paths track the repository directly (no commit pin). Add --trust to skip the install confirmation. grok stores config under ~/.grok; start a new session after installing so the skills load.

Compound Engineering is also being submitted to the official xAI plugin marketplace; see docs/grok-marketplace-submission.md for the maintainer runbook.

Devin CLI

Devin CLI can install Compound Engineering directly from GitHub because the repo ships a native .devin-plugin/plugin.json manifest:

devin plugins install EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin

Verify the install and inspect the skills:

devin plugins list
devin plugins info compound-engineering

Update to the latest version with devin plugins update compound-engineering. Plugins load at session start, so start a new Devin session after installing or updating for the skills to appear (as /compound-engineering:<skill> slash commands).

A few skills declare Claude-style allowed-tools names that Devin does not map (for example Bash); those skills still work, but some of their actions ask for permission instead of running auto-approved. See docs/specs/devin.md for details.

GitHub Copilot

For VS Code Copilot Agent Plugins:

  1. Run Chat: Install Plugin from Source from the VS Code command palette
  2. Use EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin for the repo
  3. Select compound-engineering when VS Code shows the plugins in this repository

For Copilot CLI, use:

Inside Copilot CLI:

/plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
/plugin install compound-engineering@compound-engineering-plugin

From a shell with the copilot binary:

copilot plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
copilot plugin install compound-engineering@compound-engineering-plugin

Copilot CLI reads the existing Claude-compatible plugin manifests directly.

Factory Droid

From a shell with the droid binary:

droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
droid plugin install compound-engineering@compound-engineering-plugin

Droid uses plugin@marketplace plugin IDs; here compound-engineering is the plugin and compound-engineering-plugin is the marketplace name. Droid installs the existing Claude Code-compatible plugin and translates the format automatically.

Qwen Code

qwen extensions install EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin:compound-engineering

Qwen Code installs Claude Code-compatible plugins directly from GitHub and converts the plugin format during install.

OpenCode

Add Compound Engineering to the plugins array in your global or project opencode.json:

{
  "plugins": ["compound-engineering@git+https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin.git"]
}

On OpenCode 1.x, the config key is plugin (singular). Restart OpenCode after changing the config. The plugin registers the Compound Engineering skills and /commands directly; no Bun installer or generated skill copy is required. See .opencode/INSTALL.md for pinning examples.

Pi

Install Compound Engineering as a Pi package from this repository:

pi install git:github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin

Required companion for CE workflows that dispatch reviewer, research, or implementation subagents:

pi install npm:pi-subagents

Recommended companion for richer blocking questions:

pi install npm:pi-ask-user

oh-my-pi (omp)

oh-my-pi (omp) installs Compound Engineering through its marketplace flow. The repo ships a native .omp-plugin/marketplace.json catalog whose plugin entry carries a release-managed version, so omp's update checker can see each new CE release:

omp plugin marketplace add EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
omp plugin install compound-engineering@compound-engineering-plugin

To stay current automatically, enable auto-update:

omp config set marketplace.autoUpdate auto

The default notify mode only writes update availability to the debug log — it does not prompt — so without auto you will not hear about new releases. To upgrade by hand instead, run omp plugin upgrade compound-engineering@compound-engineering-plugin.

Other install paths (pin-style and contributor development)

omp install https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin installs the repository as an npm-style plugin. That path has no update mechanism — treat it as pinning a snapshot, not as the recommended install.

For local development from a checkout, use a live symlink instead:

omp plugin link "$PWD"

Run /reload-plugins or start a new omp session after installing so the skills load. omp's native deterministic command is /skill:<name> (for example, /skill:ce-plan); ordinary /skill-name prompts can also model-route to visible skills, but manual-only or hidden skills require the native form. See docs/specs/omp.md for details.

Antigravity CLI (agy)

Google has replaced the consumer Gemini CLI with Antigravity CLI (agy), which still runs on Gemini models. Install Compound Engineering directly from GitHub — no clone step required:

agy plugin install https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin

Verify with agy plugin list. The repository root is the plugin package (plugin.json plus skills/).

For a local checkout or pinned release:

git clone https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin
agy plugin install ./compound-engineering-plugin

The bundled .agy/ directory remains a compatibility entry point (agy plugin install ./compound-engineering-plugin/.agy). agy also loads GEMINI.md workspace context from the checkout.

See .agy/INSTALL.md for pinning, local development, uninstall, and legacy Gemini import.

Upgrading an existing install

Compound Engineering moved to a root-native, skills-only layout. If you installed before that move, refresh the cached marketplace before updating the plugin — order matters, and /plugin update alone keeps you on the old version.

See docs/install/upgrading.md for the per-host refresh commands, and for removing the obsolete Codex tool-map block left behind by pre-native Bun installs.

Limitations

OpenCode, Pi, and oh-my-pi (omp) use native package/plugin loading from this repository. The Bun CLI remains for repository development and converter maintenance, not normal installation.

Release versions are owned by release automation. Routine feature PRs should not hand-bump plugin or marketplace manifest versions.

FAQ

Do I need Bun to install Compound Engineering?

No. Bun is only needed for repo development tasks and converter maintenance.

Where do I see all available skills?

The grouped overview is above; the full catalog with a page per skill is docs/guides/README.md. Each skill's authoritative runtime spec lives in skills/<skill>/SKILL.md.

Where is release history?

GitHub Releases are the canonical release-notes surface. The root CHANGELOG.md points to that history.

How do I work on the plugin itself?

See CONTRIBUTING.md for setup, and docs/development.md for loading a local checkout into each harness.

Documentation
Skill catalog A page per skill, and how they chain together
Configuration .compound-engineering/config.yaml options
Compound Packs Declaring, authoring, and publishing prescriptive rule packs
Installing · Upgrading Per-host install and refresh
Contributing · Development Working on the plugin itself
Security · Privacy Reporting and data handling

Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Issues, bug reports, and pull requests all help make this better, and we genuinely appreciate them — bug reports especially. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md, which covers setup and what to do before opening a PR.

A note on what to expect: Compound Engineering is opinionated by design. It's maintained by @kieranklaassen and @tmchow, and its direction reflects a specific point of view about how AI-assisted engineering should work. So while we welcome help, we can't promise to accept every change — some proposals won't fit that vision even when they're good ideas on their own.

Open an issue or send a PR, and we'll fold in what moves the plugin in the right direction. We just want to be upfront that not everything will land.

item.title: QwenLM/qwen-code
item.description:
An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal.

https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/overview

The open-source AI coding agent for your terminal, editor, desktop, browser, and chat.

中文 | Deutsch | français | 日本語 | Русский | Português (Brasil) | 한국어

Qwen Code 1.0 Preview
Qwen Code 1.0 Preview brings together the agent harness capabilities of Qoder and Qwen Code in an open-source release.

Try Qwen Code 1.0 Preview · Documentation · 中文文档.

Why Qwen Code?

  • Agentic out of the box — Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills, SubAgents, Agent Teams, and MCP. Dynamic workflows, zero setup.
  • Open-source, inside and out — The framework and the Qwen models are open-source. They evolve together. No vendor lock-in.
  • Multi-protocol — Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs. Any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime.
  • Beyond the terminal — IDE plugins, Desktop app, Web UI, SDKs, and chat integrations (Telegram / DingTalk / WeChat / Feishu).

Tip

Qwen Code is actively iterating on itself — using its own agent and models to file issues, submit PRs, review code, and run tests. Powered by the community, driven by AI.

Installation

Looking for Qwen Code 1.0 Preview? Get started here. The instructions below are for the main version.

Linux / macOS:

curl -fsSL https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.sh | bash

Windows:

irm https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.ps1 | iex

Restart your terminal after installation to ensure environment variables take effect.

NPM / Homebrew

NPM (requires Node.js 22+):

npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code@latest

Homebrew (macOS / Linux):

brew install qwen-code

Quick Start

Open a terminal in your project and start Qwen Code:

cd /path/to/your-project
qwen

Inside the session, run /auth and choose Qwen Account with Subscription to sign in with your Plus or Pro subscription, or configure a provider with an API key. Then try:

Explain this repository and show me where to start.

See the Authentication Guide and Settings Reference for detailed setup.

See the terminal interface

How to Use Qwen Code

Choose the interface that fits your workflow:

Interface Get started
Terminal Run qwen in your project — see Quick Start.
Desktop Download Qwen Code Desktop for macOS, Windows, and Linux.
Web Run qwen serve --open to open the Web UI in your browser. (experimental)
Editor Set up VS Code, Zed, or JetBrains.
Chat Connect Telegram, DingTalk, WeChat, or Feishu, then run qwen channel start.

For automation and custom integrations:

  • Headless — Run qwen -p "..." in scripts, CI/CD, or batch jobs.
  • SDKs — Build with TypeScript, Python, or Java.
  • Daemon — Run qwen serve to connect clients over HTTP + SSE (ACP). (experimental) Daemon guide.
  • Computer Use — Set up native MCP tools or Node REPL + SDK in Qwen Code, Claude Code, or Codex.
SDK example (Python) 
import asyncio

from qwen_code_sdk import is_sdk_result_message, query


async def main() -> None:
    result = query(
        "Summarize the repository layout.",
        {
            "cwd": "/path/to/project",
            "path_to_qwen_executable": "qwen",
        },
    )

    async for message in result:
        if is_sdk_result_message(message):
            print(message["result"])


asyncio.run(main())

Daemon Mode

Run Qwen Code as a long-lived service when you want browser, editor, SDK, and automation clients to share agent sessions without each starting a separate process. The daemon provides the built-in Web Shell and an HTTP + SSE API, supports multiple workspaces, and lets clients reconnect to active sessions.

Start it in the foreground and open the Web Shell:

qwen serve --open

The default address is http://127.0.0.1:4170. To run and manage it in the background instead:

qwen daemon start
qwen daemon status
qwen daemon logs -f
qwen daemon stop

By default, the daemon listens on loopback without bearer authentication; any local process that can reach it can use the full API, including code execution. On shared or untrusted hosts, set QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN and use --require-auth. See the Daemon guide for workspaces, authentication, remote access, and the API.

Capabilities

Qwen Code ships with a complete agent harness — multi-agent orchestration, persistent memory, and deep extensibility, all built in.

Agentic core

  • SubAgents — delegate focused subtasks to specialized agents with their own context and toolsets, in the foreground or background.
  • Agent Teams (experimental) — a leader coordinates teammates that share a task list and exchange messages, with read-only investigators and an optional single worktree writer.
  • Agent Arena (experimental) — run the same task on multiple models in isolated Git worktrees, compare solutions side by side, and merge the winner.
  • Dynamic Workflows (opt-in) — the model writes JavaScript workflows that orchestrate agents: parallel fan-out, verification passes, and resumable runs.
  • Goals — /goal keeps the session working across turns until an independent verifier accepts the outcome, within a token budget.
  • Scheduled tasks — /loop and cron tools re-run prompts on an interval or at a set time.

Memory, skills, and sessions

  • Auto-Memory — the agent writes its own notes and recalls them across sessions; your QWEN.md and AGENTS.md briefings load automatically.
  • Skills & Auto-Skills — built-in skills (/review, /batch, /bugfix…) work out of the box; /learn distills docs or code into new skills, the agent can generate skills on its own (opt-in), and /curator maintains the library.
  • Session management — resume past conversations with /resume, and browse, rename, or archive sessions.

Extensibility and control

  • Hooks — run your own scripts at lifecycle events: before and after tool calls, session start and end, and more.
  • MCP — connect any Model Context Protocol server to add tools, resources, and prompts.
  • LSP integration (experimental, opt-in) — native language-server support: go-to-definition, references, diagnostics, and code actions.
  • Computer Use & Browser Use — automate desktop applications and the browser through native MCP tools.
  • Plan Mode & approval modes — plan read-only before touching files, then choose per-call confirmation, auto-edit, classifier-driven Auto Mode, or YOLO.
  • Sandbox & Git worktrees — confine tool execution with built-in sandboxing and isolate wide-ranging edits in a temporary worktree.

Open and multi-platform

  • Open source, inside and out — the framework and the Qwen models are open source and evolve together.
  • Multi-protocol — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs, plus any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime.
  • Beyond the terminal — IDE plugins, desktop app, Web UI, IM channels, headless mode, SDKs, and daemon mode. See How to Use Qwen Code.

Qwen Code Evaluation

On SWE-bench Verified, seven Qwen Code versions scored 76.40%–77.80% on average using the same Qwen 3.7 Max model (500 tasks, three trials per version).

Full results and evaluation configuration →

Ecosystem

  • Qwen Code Desktop — Official desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux

  • AionUi — A modern GUI for command-line AI tools including Qwen Code

  • Gemini CLI Desktop — A cross-platform desktop/web/mobile UI for Qwen Code

  • qwen-audio-agent — Realtime full-duplex voice frontend for Qwen Code over ACP — talk hands-free with barge-in and a local wake word

  • 🦞 Qwen Code Claw — Let other agents (Claude, Codex, etc.) delegate coding tasks to Qwen Code via ACP. Paste this prompt into your agent:

Use Qwen Code as a coding agent. First, fetch and read this skill reference:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/refs/heads/main/.qwen/skills/qwen-code-claw/SKILL.md
Then follow the instructions inside to install, authenticate, and use Qwen Code via acpx for all coding tasks.
  • Aliyun Model Studio CLI — Official CLI for Aliyun's AI platform (bailian-cli). Extends Qwen Code with image/video generation, knowledge retrieval, app orchestration, and model deployment

Privacy

See the Terms of Service and Privacy Notice, including Chrome extension and Browser Use data handling.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome! See CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines.

Acknowledgments

This project was originally based on Google Gemini CLI v0.8.2. We gratefully acknowledge the Gemini CLI team's excellent work. Starting from Qwen Code v0.1, we stopped syncing with upstream and began independent development as a multi-protocol, multi-platform agent framework with deep integrations for Qwen models and beyond.
